key_decisions.decision: CPU register interface and register set
key_decisions.ma_choice: Plain 32-bit register port (addr[4:0], wdata, we, re, registered rdata) with an OpenCores-style PRESC/CTRL/TXR/RXR/CMD/STATUS map
key_decisions.plan_choice: Same plain register port and OpenCores-style map, settled by the Q1 answer
key_decisions.note: The spec said TBD; the plan asked and got the answer.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Byte-level CMD with STA/STO/RD/WR/ACK/IACK, any combination per byte; STA while owned gives Sr
key_decisions.plan_choice: OpenCores-style byte-level CMD with STA/STO/RD/WR/ACK/IACK; STA on a held bus gives Sr

key_decisions.ma_choice: No address hardware; firmware writes {addr,R/W} to TXR with STA|WR
Single TXR and RXR, no FIFOs
irq = IEN & IF; IF set on done/AL and cleared by CMD.IACK; STATUS holds IF/TIP/AL/BUSY/RXACK
key_decisions.plan_choice: Same OpenCores IF/IEN/IACK scheme with the same STATUS bits
key_decisions.note: The plan would also fold a timeout cause into IF.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Byte controller FSM sequencing bit-controller primitives (START/STOP/DATA)
key_decisions.plan_choice: Bit engine (S5) plus byte controller (S6) with a handshake

key_decisions.ma_choice: Single 16-bit PRESC giving quarter-period q = PRESC+1 clocks; fixed 50% duty, 4q per bit
key_decisions.plan_choice: Single 16-bit PRESC in OpenCores style (~5*(PRESC+1) per period) with fixed sub-phases
key_decisions.note: The phase granularity differs slightly (5 vs 4 phases), but both use one runtime prescaler with a fixed duty cycle.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Run Fast mode at 375 kHz (PRESC=31) because a 50% duty cycle at 400 kHz violates tLOW >= 1.3 us
key_decisions.plan_choice: Plan requires checking tLOW against the fixed duty cycle and stating a reduced Fm SCL if 400 kHz is not compliant
key_decisions.note: The plan anticipates the issue without fixing the number.

key_decisions.ma_choice: 2-FF sync plus stability filter with a runtime-programmable length in CTRL.FILT (0-7, default 3, rejects >= 50 ns)
key_decisions.plan_choice: 2-FF sync plus digital filter whose length is a synthesis parameter only, with no register field
key_decisions.note: This changes the CTRL register contents and removes firmware tunability.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Separate scl_i/scl_oe and sda_i/sda_oe (oe=1 drives low); never drive high; pad outside the IP
Single peripheral clock domain; only SCL/SDA synchronized
SCL-release phases wait for filtered SCL high before counting; also gives multi-master clock sync
key_decisions.plan_choice: Freeze the phase counter until filtered SCL reads high on every rising edge
key_decisions.note: The MA also ends the high phase early if another master pulls SCL low; the plan only mentions clock sync implicitly.

key_decisions.ma_choice: bus_busy tracked from START/STOP detection; STA waits in idle until STOP when another master owns the bus
key_decisions.plan_choice: BUSY set by START and cleared by STOP; STA waits while busy

key_decisions.ma_choice: Detect SDA mismatch in DATA/START/STOP and a foreign STOP; release lines immediately, set AL and IF, abort, no retry
key_decisions.plan_choice: Detect SDA mismatch or an unexpected START/STOP; release both lines, abort, set AL and IF, no auto-retry

key_decisions.ma_choice: No timeouts; recommended for a later revision
key_decisions.plan_choice: Add a programmable timeout register at a spare offset (0 = disabled) that aborts and sets a STATUS timeout bit plus IF
key_decisions.note: Adds a register and a STATUS bit, so the interface and error behaviour change.

key_decisions.ma_choice: Slave NACK only reported in RXACK; no automatic abort or STOP
key_decisions.plan_choice: NACK does not abort; firmware decides on STOP

summary: The plan lines up closely with the MA. It has the same OpenCores-style byte-level programming model, plain register port, single TXR/RXR, IF/IEN/IACK interrupt and two-layer bit/byte engine. It also agrees on single-PRESC timing, stretching through SCL readback, STA waiting while the bus is busy, and immediate release on arbitration loss. It even anticipates the Fast-mode tLOW/duty-cycle problem. There are two material differences. The plan makes the glitch filter a synthesis-time parameter, whereas the MA puts a runtime CTRL.FILT field in the register map. The plan also adds a programmable timeout register and STATUS bit that the MA deliberately leaves out. The only question asked (CPU interface) was legitimately open in the spec.
